about: Hero props and materials, decided by the RAG method: for each prop, the model weighs its scenes, transfers and retrieved screenplay passages ('why_hero' / 'why_not' are its reasons). Counts and totals are computed by code. Written by scripts/extract_hero_props.py.

per_scene.scene: EXT. SABA ELIOR’S COURTYARD — LATE MORNING

hero_props.name: Cloth bundle
hero_props.description: small cloth bundle held close to Miri’s chest
why_hero: Miri carries the cloth bundle from the opening, clutched to her chest, and it is revealed to hold the three honey-date cakes.
It recurs across the story: Miri touches or opens it in scenes 1, 2, 15, and 16.
The cloth becomes the container for the cakes when Miri closes it around them in scene 15, supporting the cake-giving plot.
hero_props.story_role: the carrier for Miri’s honey-date cakes

hero_props.name: Honey-date cakes
hero_props.description: three small honey-date cakes gleaming in the cloth
why_hero: The cakes recur from the morning bundle through the scroll room inventory to the sunset sharing scene.
Miri withholds them from Tav early because they are for Saba, then later gives Tav one whole cake and half of another.
The final division with Tav, Nim, and Miri is called “emotionally significant” and resolves as a generous gesture.

hero_props.name: Small scroll
adjectives: tied with a cord the color of barley
hero_props.description: a small scroll tied with a cord the color of barley
why_hero: Saba deliberately selects and unties it in the Scroll Room, and its loaf-and-two-fish seal makes Nim react as if it matters.
Its ink glimmers when opened, then later settles into a drawing of five loaves and two fish, tying it to the later lunch imagery.
It recurs open between Miri and Nim in scene 15, making it more than background scroll-room dressing.
hero_props.story_role: the prophetic scroll of the five loaves and two fish

hero_props.name: Yonah's bundle
hero_props.description: small bundle tucked under his arm, packed with five barley loaves and two fish
why_hero: The bundle is introduced with Yonah carrying it carefully, then identified as the five loaves and two fish that can answer the hungry crowd.
It is unwrapped and featured in scene 9, with the screenplay listing the contents plainly: five small barley loaves and two small fish.
It is passed from Yonah to Andrew, then from Andrew to Jesus, with Jesus’s hands specifically shown receiving the small lunch.
hero_props.story_role: the small lunch offered for the feeding miracle

hero_props.name: Barley loaves
why_hero: The loaves are explicitly identified as Yonah’s scarce lunch in scene 9: “Five barley loaves and two fish… definitely not enough,” then Andrew receives it with care.
Jesus lifts the loaves in scene 11, after which they appear as “warm barley loaves, enough for many,” making them central to the miracle.
They recur across scenes 8, 9, and 11 and are passed from Yonah toward Andrew/Jesus, then become food Miri distributes to the children.
hero_props.story_role: the humble lunch multiplied to feed many

hero_props.name: Bread basket
why_hero: Jesus briefly rests His hand on the bread basket in scene 10 as He commits to feeding everyone: “All of them.”
In scene 11, the basket is central to the multiplication set piece: bread appears beyond what should be there and “the basket remains full.”
It is passed hand to hand, including Andrew placing a basket in Miri’s hands, and becomes part of the visible abundance later gathered as twelve full baskets.
hero_props.story_role: the basket of miraculous bread that feeds the crowd

hero_props.name: Broken bread
hero_props.description: pieces of the multiplied barley bread
why_hero: The bread is central to the miracle: in scene 11 there is “more bread than should be there,” it is handed onward, and the basket remains full.
It is repeatedly passed and gathered: Miri distributes it to children, elders, fathers, and mothers, then Miri, Yonah, and Nim gather leftovers into baskets in scene 13.
It carries the theme of abundance and not keeping for oneself, shown when Miri places her leftover piece in the basket instead of saving it.
hero_props.story_role: the multiplied bread that feeds the crowd and embodies abundance

hero_props.name: Toy cart
hero_props.description: Tav's broken toy cart with a badly wobbling wheel
why_hero: The cart recurs from scene 2, where Tav is disappointed Miri leaves it broken, to scene 16, where he asks her to help with the wheel.
Its repair creates a small emotional payoff: Nim sacrifices a peg and Miri fixes the wheel so the cart rolls straight.
The screenplay explicitly frames the moment as “small, but emotionally significant.”
hero_props.story_role: Tav’s broken toy that lets Miri and Nim show care

hero_props.name: Toy cart wheel
hero_props.description: the wobbling wheel on Tav's toy cart
why_hero: The wheel recurs from scene 2, where Tav's cart is broken and Miri leaves it, to scene 16, where Tav asks Miri for help.
Miri fixes the wobbling wheel with Nim's small peg, and the cart rolling straight provides a visible payoff.
The repair reflects the giving/helping theme, with Nim sacrificing the peg and Miri choosing to help Tav.
hero_props.story_role: the broken toy part Miri repairs to show generosity

hero_props.name: Small peg
hero_props.description: a small peg for securing the toy cart wheel
why_hero: Nim passes the small peg to Miri in scene 16, making it a deliberate exchanged object rather than set dressing.
Miri uses it to secure Tav’s toy cart wheel, resolving the earlier broken/wobbly cart setup from scenes 2 and 16.
Nim frames giving the peg as a sacrifice, so it supports the scene’s emotional beat of generosity.
hero_props.story_role: the tiny gift that fixes Tav’s cart wheel
